title: Limiting reactant and yield: reducing iron(III) oxide
promptMarkdown:
Iron(III) oxide is reduced by carbon monoxide:
$$\ce{Fe2O3(s) + 3 CO(g) -> 2 Fe(s) + 3 CO2(g)}$$
(check that it is balanced before using it). A virtual run starts with $25.0\ \text{g}$ of $\ce{Fe2O3}$ and $15.0\ \text{g}$ of $\ce{CO}$ and produces $15.2\ \text{g}$ of iron. Atomic masses: Fe 55.85, C 12.01, O 16.00 $\text{g mol}^{-1}$.

1. Identify the limiting reactant, showing the comparison of amounts you used.
2. Compute the theoretical yield of iron in grams.
3. Compute the percent yield.
4. Under the theoretical complete-reaction model, compute the mass of excess CO left after all limiting reactant is consumed. Explain why the recovered 15.2 g of iron alone does not determine the actual CO remaining.
5. State the assumptions behind the theoretical yield, and give one reason a real yield could fall short that is not a calculation error.
hintLadder: Convert both masses to moles first. Masses cannot be compared directly because the molar masses differ.
Ask how many moles of $\ce{CO}$ would be needed to consume all of the $\ce{Fe2O3}$, and compare that with the moles of $\ce{CO}$ available.
The theoretical yield comes from the limiting reactant alone, through the mole ratio to iron.
The excess remaining is the amount available minus the amount consumed, converted back to grams.

deterministicChecks.description: the theoretical yield of iron is about 17.49 g (17.5 g)

checkExamples.label: correct answer
checkExamples.text: n(Fe2O3) = 25.0/159.70 = 0.1565 mol; n(CO) = 15.0/28.01 = 0.5355 mol. All the Fe2O3 needs 3 × 0.1565 = 0.4696 mol CO, less than the 0.5355 mol available, so Fe2O3 is the limiting reactant and CO is in excess. Fe theoretical: 2 × 0.1565 = 0.3131 mol × 55.85 = 17.49 g. Percent yield = 15.2/17.49 = 86.9%. Excess CO: (0.5355 − 0.4696) × 28.01 = 1.85 g. Assumes pure reactants and complete reaction as written; a real shortfall could come from incomplete reduction or losses in recovering the iron.

checkExamples.label: masses compared instead of moles
checkExamples.text: CO is the limiting reactant because 15.0 g is less than 25.0 g. Theoretical iron = 29.9 g, so the yield is 50.8%.
